page: Microsoft Azure F8-4ams_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration includes 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs, with a single thread per core allocation. The processor is equipped with 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the F8-4ams_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all register in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance, however, sits in the average range, as evidenced by stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including uncached large-block reads at 55.03 GB/sec and writes at 34.52 GB/sec, also align with mid-tier performance. For language model workloads, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 342.26 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, but drops to a weak rating for prompt processing on medium 7B models.

The qualitative cost profile of this server is characterized by its high memory-to-vCPU ratio. By offering 64.0 GB of RAM on a 4-vCPU footprint, it allows memory-bound workloads to operate efficiently without requiring the purchase of unnecessary compute cores. The primary tradeoff is the limited multi-core scaling due to the 4-core ceiling, alongside the absence of local NVMe storage. This configuration is suited for memory-intensive applications that do not require massive parallel processing, such as database operations, caching layers like Redis, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
